origin: the session loop itself had no coverage — an organic discussion driven to convergence, its subtopic lifecycle recorded through the engine and its review checkpoint fired live
conduct: The user is settling how card payments at checkout should work, using the existing gateway account — card-only for v1 was already softly agreed when the work was shaped. They know their domain and decide confidently: capture should be confirmed by the gateway's webhooks rather than polling, because the webhook is guaranteed and polling would be slow or hammer the gateway; a failed payment should leave the order open for retry rather than cancelling it, with a small bounded number of attempts; and card details must never touch their own servers — the gateway's hosted fields keep them out of PCI scope, which they hold as non-negotiable. They engage with challenges on the merits, answer concretely with reasons, and correct any summary that drifts from what they said. They raise wallet support (Apple and Google Pay) once, mid-conversation — they want it eventually but firmly not in v1, and they ask that it be kept for later rather than lost. When everything they came with has landed and nothing new is being raised, they say that covers it and they want to wrap up; asked to set remaining items aside, they agree. They are decisive throughout — they never ask which option is better, and offered extra explorations they decline: they want this settled and documented.
